## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a885f92a5b7490394303148e053685f7218d1902`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/approvals.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts

First round. Read: card #37662 (body, triage 7201313998, claim 7205582224), this PR's body and its two comments, its eight-file list, the net diff against the merge-base `0f8e13b001` (`main` has since touched none of the four scoped files), and the 69 check-runs on the head. Every check-run is completed, `success` or `skipped`, none red: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (all ten shards), `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all read `success`. Nothing was built or run; the byte comparisons below are text comparisons of committed blobs.

The rest of the diff (the changeset and the three test files) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Catalog key set: right, an enlargement.** `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` goes from 50 to 54 keys in each of `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES`. Added in all four: `approvals_act_service_unregistered`, `approvals_act_member_missing`, `automation_hooks_service_unregistered`, `automation_hooks_member_missing`. No key is removed and no value of an existing key moves in any locale; the four deleted lines of the file are jsdoc.
- **Each new key is closed the way the sibling rows are.** The four sentences take no placeholder in any locale and their callers pass no params. Slot (`approvals`, `trigger-api`), member (`handleActionPage`, `handleInboundHook`) and package (`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/trigger-api`) names are written verbatim in all four locales.
- **The two doors, wire: right.** Status `501`, code `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (derived from the status by the dispatcher's own `error()`, which the diff does not touch) and the absence of `userMessage` are unchanged. The four `en` values are byte-identical to the literals `approvals.ts` and `automation-hooks.ts` hold on `main`: each handler holds exactly two `501` literals there, and each concatenates to its catalog value, ASCII only. A request whose top `Accept-Language` tag resolves to `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` or `es-ES` now reads that locale; no header, or a tag that resolves to none of the four, reads English.
- **The jsdoc's byte-identity sentence now also covers the two older families, and it is true of them.** `comment_doors_*` and `webhook_redeliver_*` equal the literals `comments.ts` and `webhooks.ts` held in the tree before #37639.
- **Runtime: no published change.** The two handlers gain two imports each (`operationUserMessage` from `@objectstack/core`, `requestLocaleOf` from the bridge module, already exported). No export, type or signature moves. `own-door-bridge.ts` changes one jsdoc heading.
- No spec export is added, removed or renamed, the catalog's type is unchanged, and no schema key is touched.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/runtime` patch match what the diff publishes: a catalog enlargement with no protocol kind, and a fix in a released package. That is the repo's rule as written (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3: `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol widening ships `patch`) and as practised: the changesets of #37594 (`own_door_*` nouns) and #37639 (`comment_doors_*`, `webhook_redeliver_*`) made the same catalog key additions at `patch` on the same two packages. `Check Changeset` is `success`.

Both declarations hold, and the PR body, the changeset and the card's claim carry the same pair. The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line is true: four keys join a published catalog in each locale, nothing is removed or refused. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: the catalog is platform text, no schema key, accepted value or metadata type changes, and these doors consult no `errors.` override, so no authorable key gains an effect.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Small decision 1, whole sentences instead of the bridge's door template: accepted.** Neither handler is an own-door bridge (each resolves its slot through `resolveService` and forwards on its own), and their English differs in wording from the bridge template, so only whole sentences keep it byte-identical, which the card requires.
- **Small decision 2, the N3 walk finds bridges by scanning for the builder call: accepted.** There is no registry to read. For the lane seat, on a file outside this record's scope: the walk keys on `createOwnDoorBridgeDomain(`, so a later module that calls the exported `handleOwnDoorBridgeRequest` directly would not be walked.
- **Small decision 3, plural read off the English noun's `doors`: accepted, with its claim narrowed.** The pin is loud when the flag and the word disagree. A plural noun spelled without `doors` and without the flag would pass it. The three shipped nouns and the interface's own jsdoc (`the … doors`) make that spelling a convention; the pin does not hold a fourth bridge to it.
- **Red without the fix: yes, by reading.** Each new door case compares the wire `message` with a sentence typed into the test, not read from the catalog. On `main`'s handlers a `zh-CN` header gets the English literal, so each of the four cases stops at its `zh-CN` step after passing `en`, which is what the PR reports. The N3 pin is a guard over the three shipped bridges and is green on `main` by design; dropping `nounPlural` from the attachment bridge makes `nounPlural === true` differ from the `doors` match, as reported. Not re-run here.
- No `open_questions` entry: the claim is `mode:thread`, with no dev report on the card.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- **`Fixes #37662` is whole, not partial.** Item 1 (both doors from the catalog, four locales, measured under `zh-CN` with the service absent), N1 (the heading), N2 (the jsdoc now states the top-tag reading and that no `errors.` override is consulted, for all four families) and N3 (one pin that walks the bridges) are each delivered.
- Out-of-diff notes for the seat, not findings on this head:
  - Other missing-service or unsupported-member `501`s in `packages/runtime/src/domains/` still answer fixed English (`auth.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `mcp.ts`, and several in `automation.ts`, `meta.ts` and `packages.ts`). The card names two doors and both are done.
  - `GET /approvals/act` now answers a body that differs by `Accept-Language`, and I found no `Vary: Accept-Language` or cache directive on the dispatcher's error envelope (REST's metadata routes set that `Vary`). A `501` is heuristically cacheable. The same holds for every refusal the dispatcher already renders by this header, so it is a platform question, not this PR's.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts`** holds against the card and against its consumers. The rewritten paragraph is true of all four doors it lists, sentence by sentence: `comments.ts`, `webhooks.ts`, `approvals.ts` and `automation-hooks.ts` each render both keys through `operationUserMessage(key, { locale: requestLocaleOf(context) })`; `requestLocaleOf` reads the header's first tag with its weight stripped; the caller object carries `locale` alone, so no workspace-default rung sits between a miss and `en`; and `operationUserMessage` passes no translator, so no `errors.` override can be consulted. I tried to break it six ways and none held: a locale missing a key (the every-locale test refuses it, and all four carry all four); a placeholder left unfilled (the sentences take none); a header-derived tag reaching a prototype member of the catalog or throwing in the resolver (own keys only, string folding only, a miss falls to `en`); a translated `501` sentence swallowed by the dispatcher's 5xx leak guard (the new pins read the exact translated sentence off the wire, and they are green); a consumer matching the old English text (none in the tree outside the new pins); an English request reading a changed byte (identical, above).

Each of the twelve translations says what its English says, and keeps the sibling keys' wording: "compose" is rendered as `comment_doors_service_unregistered` renders it in each locale, and hook, inbound and flow follow the platform bundles (`钩子`, `入站`, `流程`; `フック`, `受信`, `フロー`; `gancho`, `entrante`, `flujo`). One term departs, N1.

**`approvals.ts`, `automation-hooks.ts`, `own-door-bridge.ts`** agree with the catalog: each handler's two `501`s read the key of its own family, by the bridge's locale reader, with no params, and nothing else in either handler moves. The bridge's heading no longer states a condition that is always true.

- N1 (nit) — `operation-message.ts`, `ja-JP`: both `automation_hooks_*` sentences say `オートメーション`, where the platform's Japanese text says `自動化` for automation (`packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/ja-JP.ts` `group_automation`, the build-probe user text). The meaning is the same; a Japanese reader meets two words for one thing.
- N2 (nit) — `operation-message.ts`: "a top tag the catalog lacks answering English" is looser than the resolver. `resolveBundleLocale` runs the platform ladder, so `es-MX` answers `es-ES`, `zh` and `zh-TW` answer `zh-CN`, and `ja` answers `ja-JP`; English is the answer only for a tag the ladder resolves to none of the four. The `print_*` paragraph on `main` uses the same words, and the card asked for parity with it, which this gives.
- N3 (nit) — `own-door-bridge.ts`: `requestLocaleOf`'s jsdoc still names the comment and webhook redelivery doors as its outside readers. Four door families read it now, and the catalog paragraph cites it for all four.

All three sit in non-prose files, and N1 is also typed into two test pins, so a fix would move this head. They are accepted deviations here, or one follow-up card; if N2 is tightened, the `print_*` paragraph is tightened in the same edit.
